question: Explain the BCG growth-share matrix and its use in portfolio analysis.

points.label: Axes
points.description: Business units are placed on a grid of market growth rate (vertical) and relative market share (horizontal).

points.label: Stars
points.description: High growth and high share; they need heavy investment to keep growing and may become cash cows later.

points.label: Cash cows
points.description: Low growth but high share; they generate more cash than they need, which funds other units.

points.label: Question marks
points.description: High growth but low share; they need cash and a decision whether to invest to build share or to drop them.

points.label: Dogs and use of the matrix
points.description: Dogs have low growth and low share and are candidates for harvesting or divestment; the matrix helps balance the portfolio and allocate resources among units.
points.basis: BCG matrix: dogs and portfolio strategies
